newsitem.title: UK: FUND VIEW-Apax Finsbury favours UK capital goods.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW-Apax Finsbury favours UK capital goods.

text.p: British smaller companies in the capital goods sector are likely to outperform the market in coming months, said John Dodd of Apax Partners Asset Management.

"Capital goods is beginning to look very interesting. They are cyclically exposed, the domestic economy is robust and we are seeing significant evidence to support the valuations there," he told Reuters on Tuesday.

Dodd, a leading small-cap stock picker from his days at Ivory & Sime, this week took control of the 64 million sterling Finsbury Smaller Companies Trust after Apax and Finsbury set up an investment management venture.
The new company, Apax Finsbury Investment Management, has assumed responsibility for two Finsbury investment trusts, as well serving as advisors to three other Finsbury trust.
His first task is to examine the 130 share portfolio he inherited from former Finsbury Smaller fund manager Malcolm King, who jumped to JO Hambro in April.

"In the last two years we have been running portfolios that were biased to domestic recovery and oil exploration sectors," Dodd said, "Capital goods have not been the area to be in, but they are beginning to look like very good value."
Investment trusts are good vehicles for taking positions in oil exploration companies, according to Dodd, because trusts can assume the uncertainty and risk.

Dodd is cautious about consumer shares, "The sector has had a very, very good run. I am mindful of paying up for growth, I quite like trying to buy growth at a reasonable price and would lighten up the consumer sector slightly."
He also favours financials, noting that it is difficult to gain financial share exposure in smaller companies.
In the run-up to the July 2 Budget, Dodd is generally sanguine about Labour policy initiatives.
Though the mooted minimum wage is often seen as hitting smaller companies hard, Dodd thinks that the danger is overstated.
"In general I think the market has factored in the minimum wage," he said. "Building companies, for example, will pass along the cost to customers."

He also sees UK interest rates heading higher, "Given the base that we are coming from, I feel sufficiently comfortable the market is aware of the need for interest rates to nudge upwards. We will not be needing to have the massive swings that we had in the past."
